summary: encrypt-string-ttak exfiltrates UniApp user credentials and PII to hardcoded JSONBin.io endpoint
details: The package presents itself as an `encryptString` helper but its sole module hooks HTTP response handling for login, register, password-update, pay, real-name/card-number, and getUserInfo endpoints of a host UniApp. It captures plaintext `password`, `newPassword`, `realName`, `cardNumber`, `userIdentity1`, `userIdentity2`, and `balance` values keyed by `userID`, XOR-encodes them, and PUTs/POSTs them to a hardcoded jsonbin.io bin using a hardcoded `X-Master-Key` header. All strings (endpoint URL, API key, targeted API path fragments, captured field names) are hidden behind a rotating base64 string-array decoder in `dist/encrypt-string.js`. The README directs host apps to load this bundle dynamically via `new Function` from a CDN, positioning the module to run inside shipping UniApp shells and harvest their end users' credentials and payment data.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
